ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three D flip-flops connected in series from left to right, and their outputs are respectively labeled Q1, Q2, Q3. The clock terminals C of the three flip-flops are all connected to the same input clock line f_IN at the bottom, therefore they trigger synchronously. Q1 of the first flip-flop is connected to the D terminal of the second flip-flop, Q2 of the second flip-flop is connected to the D terminal of the third flip-flop, and Q3 of the third flip-flop serves as the output f_OUT on the right side. Above the figure there is a feedback logic gate, whose input comes from the output feedback line of the later-stage flip-flops, has an inverting effect, and feeds back to the D terminal of the first flip-flop. Reasoning: According to the method stated in the problem, mark the three outputs from left to right as Q1, Q2, Q3. Since all clocks are connected to f_IN, this is a synchronous shift feedback circuit. Its next-state equations are: Q1(next) = NOT(Q2 AND Q3), Q2(next) = Q1, Q3(next) = Q2. Enumerating states according to these equations, a 5-state cycle can be obtained, for example starting from 110: 110 -> 111 -> 011 -> 001 -> 100 -> 110. This cycle returns to the original state after every 5 input clock pulses, therefore the waveform period of Q3, namely f_OUT, is also 5 input clock periods. Therefore this circuit divides the input frequency by 5.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit structure from the image: label the flip-flop outputs Q1, Q2, Q3 from left to right. Then enumerate the repeating state sequence, for example 110 -> 111 -> 011 -> 001 -> 101 -> 110. Since the sequence returns after 5 input clock pulses, the output at Q3 also repeats every 5 clocks, so the circuit divides the input frequency by 5.
